title: Threat Detection Library - FortiGate Privileged Admin Action Validation Entry
description: Schema for a single entry in data/fortigate-privileged-admin-validations.json -- this library's second validation catalogue, alongside data/rhel-privileged-action-validations.json. Not a production detection rule: its 'search' field is a one-shot presence check ('did the expected event show up'), and its distinguishing fields (safe_test, test_step, rollback_step, test_result) describe executing an action once against a controlled FortiGate device and confirming the telemetry/detection fired. See docs/validations.md for the full rationale.

id.description: Stable catalogue identifier, sourced from the original workbook's Event ID column.

platform.description: Platform(s) this validation applies to. Every entry in this catalogue is FortiGate-scoped today. "FortiGate" matches the exact fortinet_product value data/fortinet-detections.json already uses for the same device.

category.description: Original test grouping, e.g. Administrator, Firewall Policy, IPsec VPN.

event_type.description: High-level privileged activity taxonomy, e.g. Administrator management, Firewall policy management, VPN administration.

title.description: Canonical description of the privileged action.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the action (the workbook's Examples column).

privilege_level.description: Expected privilege context, e.g. super_admin or delegated admin.

mitre_attack.description: Resolved against the live MITRE ATT&CK STIX corpus at conversion time -- not copied verbatim from the workbook's ATT&CK Tactic column, which still used the pre-split 'Defense Evasion' tactic name, and not from its ATT&CK Technique column, three of whose values were revoked/renumbered technique IDs (T1562, T1562.001, T1562.004) redirected via MITRE's own revoked-by relationship. A minority of entries (those with no technique to anchor a lookup, or a free-text guess with no real technique ID) may have an empty tactics/techniques array rather than a guessed mapping.

note.description: Optional context note from the source workbook, e.g. 'context dependent' or a MITRE renumbering redirect.

primary_telemetry.description: Primary FortiGate telemetry expected to record the action.

safe_test.description: Whether this action is suitable for controlled testing without intentional disruptive impact.

test_step.description: Command or action used to generate the event.

test_result.description: Pass/Fail/Partial/Not Tested tracking field -- set by whoever actually runs the validation, not by this library.

fortigate_cli_context.description: The FortiOS CLI config context the action is performed under, e.g. 'config system admin'.

expected_config_path.description: Expected FortiOS configuration path touched by the action.

expected_log_type_subtype.description: Expected FortiGate log type/subtype, e.g. 'event; system; admin'.

expected_source_ip.description: Expected management client source IP where applicable.

expected_interface_ui.description: Expected access interface, e.g. GUI(https), SSH, console, API, FortiManager.

expected_command_change.description: Expected command/configuration change recorded in telemetry.

expected_fields.description: Minimum fields useful for validation and detection.

validation_spl.description: Starter SPL to validate event presence in Splunk -- a presence check, not a tuned detection rule.
